newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Ind Minister says happy with weaker crown.
newsitem.headline: Czech Ind Minister says happy with weaker crown.

text.p: Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said on Tuesday he was satisfied with the current decline of the Czech crown but would like to see exchange rate stabilisation at an appropriate level.

"I cannot say I would consider it a bad development at the moment. A strengthening would be a very bad development. We wanted the crown to get into the depreciation band. However, I would like it to stabilise at a certain level," Dlouhy told a news conference.
The crown is allowed to fluctuate within plus or minus 7.5 percent of the midpoint of a basket made up of 65 percent marks and 35 percent dollars.

It reached a high of plus 5.5 percent against the basket mid-point earlier this year and touched a low of minus 3.8 percent on Monday, driven by speculation about an interest rate cut and generally bearish sentiment on the Czech economy.

The Czech National Bank, which is independent, successfully talked up the crown when it hit minus 3.8 percent, stressing that no interest rate cut was being discussed and it would support the crown, if necessary.
Dlouhy told reporters the market should be left to decide the appropriate level but added that a rate close to the bottom part of the fluctuation band would not be desirable.
"A fall to the bottom border of the band could have some inflationary effects," he said.
The crown stood at minus 2.68 percent versus the basket on Tuesday at 1215 GMT, up from early morning levels of around minus 3.3 percent.
The minister said stabilisation of the crown "quite low" under the basket mid-point might allow for the abolition of administrative import restrictions imposed by the cabinet two weeks ago.

As part of a recent package designed to boost growth and cut the trade deficit, the government imposed a requirement on importers of consumer and agricultural goods that they deposit 20 percent of the value of their imports in non-interest bearing accounts at Czech banks.
The Czech Statistical Bureau said last week that March's trade deficit was 13.429 billion crowns compared with 13.415 in February.
